title: Offered once to bear the sins of many
author: Hebrews
lines: so Christ also, having been offered once to bear the sins of many,
will appear a second time, without sin,
to those who are eagerly waiting for him for salvation.
why: The letter to the Hebrews in one sentence: the sacrifices of the Day of Atonement were repeated every year, but Christ was 'offered once', for good. It is the line the first Christians used to explain why there were no more sacrifices.

title: A ransom for many
author: Mark
lines: For the Son of Man also came not to be served,
and to give his life as a ransom for many.
why: Jesus's own explanation of his death, given to friends who were arguing about who was greatest. It joins the two halves of his life: he came to serve, and the service went as far as giving his life to set others free.

title: While we were yet sinners
author: Paul the Apostle
lines: But God commends his own love toward us,
in that while we were yet sinners,
why: Paul's answer to anyone who thinks the cross was God's way of loving people once they were good enough. The love came first, while we were still in the wrong. Every account of the cross has to fit this verse.

title: Him who knew no sin
author: Paul the Apostle
lines: For him who knew no sin
he made to be sin on our behalf;
so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.
why: The great exchange in one sentence: the one with no sin takes our place, so that we may take his. Luther built the Reformation's picture of the cross on it, and it is the hardest and most debated verse in this journey.
